text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London took a downward turn by the finish on Friday on light hedge selling but conditions were extremely dull. May ended down $15 at $1,565 a tonne, after a high of $1,595. The second month July contract also finished $15 easier at $1,570 a tonne. Origin sellers have stepped back, awaiting for more lucrative values, while roaster stocks have risen to more comfortable levels, resulting in a virtual standstill on the futures market, traders said.

Arabica futures in New York initially firmed, but trade rolling from May to July weakened the structure of the market. Some market observers expect the May contract to be liquidated in a more orderly fashion than the March contract and the premiums might not blow up to such extremes. By the close, spot May was down 1.95 cents/lb at 189.10 cents/lb, while second month July was down 1.60 cents/lb at 172.20 cents/lb. The outer months traded up 1.10 cents/lb to down 2.10 cents/lb.

The CSCE reported that certified stock figures were down 250 bags at 81,078 bags as of April 10. There were no bags pending grading. The Green Coffee Association figures will be released on Tuesday and if the increase is relatively minor this could spark renewed concerns about the May deliveries as well, market observers said.

BRAZIL - Brazil exported 1.53 mn 60-kg bags of coffee, ground and beans in March, above an adjusted February figure of 1.10 mn bags, the Brazilian Federation of Coffee Exporters (Febec) said. Previously Febec had estimated February exports at 1.09 mn bags. The March total is also more than twice the 583,497 bags exported in the same month in 1996. Brazilian exports so far this year have reached 3.89 mn bags, more than twice the 1.77 mn bags shipped in the first three months of 1996. Revenue more than doubled to $620.65 mn from $250.57 mn earned in January/March 1996. The average price per bag rose to $190.09 in March compared with $153.29 in February, Febec said. Of March's total, 1.51 mn bags were arabica coffee, while shipments of conillon reached 17,000 bags.

MEXICO - Mexican coffee exports totalled 651,495 60-kg bags in March, compared to the 631,513 bags shipped in the same month in 1996, the Mexican Coffee Council said. The council, the government umbrella organization covering the nation's coffee sector, said the export figure represented a 3.2 per cent rise from March 1996. The council added Mexico export figures for the first six months of the 1996/97 cycle totalled 3.235 mn bags of coffee, compared to the 2.940 mn bags in the same period for 1995/96.

UGANDA - Uganda expects exports of 4.4 mn 60-kg bags of coffee in 1996/97 (October/September) compared with 4.1 mn bags in 1995/96 but it forecasts earnings to be lower. Planning and Economic Development Minister Richard Kaijuka said in a statement that 1996/97 exports would earn Uganda $331 mn compared to $441 mn from 1995/96 exports. Kaijuka made no mention of whether Uganda would still withhold some 200,000 bags of coffee under an agreement by producers. In February African robusta coffee producers agreed on how to share out an 850,000-bag cut in exports. This followed a plan to cut world robusta exports by about 1 mn bags, approved in January by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).

UNITED STATES - For the week ended April 5, US green coffee roastings totalled approximately 290,000 60-kg bags, up from 270,000 bags the previous week and compared with 275,000 bags in the corresponding period one year-ago, Complete Coffee Coverage reports. Cumulative roastings so far totalled 4.765 mn 60-kg bags vs 4.610 mn bags in the same year-ago period.

COLOMBIA - Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation raised the country's internal coffee price by 0.8 per cent to 342,750 pesos per 125-kg load, a spokesman said. The new price, up from 339,875 pesos set on April 4 was based on an average international price of $2.03 per pound of coffee in New York, the spokesman said. The federation has now raised the internal coffee price eight times since January 31. The price has been cut twice in the same period since the federation introduced a new sliding scale formula to calculate the domestic price paid to growers.
